ruling: Eleonora, 27 October 2026, about 3:25 pm ET, chat, relayed on #1274: queue four arms on (s3c) (net settlement, a GSE-cycle ramp, spike-sized carryover, MBS settlement days), one directive each, independent of each other. hypothesis: H5 (primary goal): the SOFR - IORB spread distribution in bp. Step 3, an arm on the candidate (s3c). Development tier
target: spread_bps at the scored day, in basis points, as a 23-quantile distribution at each lead h = 1..5 (scoring_protocol.GRID)
why: (s3c) has one flat 0/1 term for the 19th to the 23rd of the month (`dom_19_23`). The cash cycle of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac runs longer: their cash comes into the market around the 19th and leaves around the 25th, and its effect may build through those days rather than stay flat.

candidate.name: sc_s3c_gse
candidate.label: (s3c-gse)
candidate.definition: (s3c) with `dom_19_23` replaced by one ramp term on the target day's calendar date: 0 before the 19th and after the 25th of the month, and on day d from the 19th to the 25th, (d - 18) / 7 (1/7 on the 19th, 4/7 on the 22nd, 1 on the 25th). Every other term, the Huber fit, the ridge of 5, the direct pairs and the SRF cap at full allotment (margin 0 bp) are (s3c)'s and stay as they are. The shape is declared before any score and is not tuned
candidate.module: repo_model.s3c_gse (ramp, GseTermTable): spread_mr_calendar.TermTable with the slot of `dom_19_23` holding the ramp at every lead and every other term the base class's; the arm is repo_model.spread_mr_state_calendar.ARMS[2] (s3) unchanged, walked on that table; the cap is repo_model.s3c_candidate.capped_quantiles, unchanged
candidate.read_at: the target day, from the target row's own date alone (no other input), on direct pairs: TermTable.read serves the row decision_index + lead, as it serves every calendar column (asof rule 2); training pairs are read from their own target rows (training_pairs = 'direct')
candidate.weekends_and_holidays: a row exists only for a business day, and its value is the ramp of its own date: when the 25th or the days before it fall on a weekend or a holiday the term is read on the business days that remain, without renumbering
candidate.count_of_the_term: a term enters a lead's fit when MIN_FLAGGED (3) training pairs carry it; the base class counts the sum of the term's values, which for the ramp is a sum of ramp values (4 for each month's 19th to 25th) and not a count of days. It passes the minimum after the first month of history, far before the first refit, so the term enters wherever the flat flag did; the page labels the sums it quotes
candidate.pairs: direct: (s3) reads the calendar columns at the target day with training_pairs = 'direct' and fit_state_terms is guarded by one_step_guard with no allow-list entry; the provisional-register row is metadata/provisional/cleared/s3c_gse_1274.json

frame.ramp_walk: (s3) is walked once on GseTermTable over every decision day from the start of the panel to the last day with five targets on or before 2026-09-03, refit every 21 decision days, direct pairs: the schedule of the frames' own walks, of which each window's is a prefix, so a window takes the walk's forecasts on its own decision days
frame.reproduction: (s3) is walked again on the base table over the same days, and its forecasts on every scored decision day of both windows must equal the frames' own (s3), cell for cell: the script refuses to write a record otherwise. This shows the ramp walk is the frames' walk with one column changed; the pooled means of (s3) and (s3c) are also compared with docs/research/s3c-candidate-1255/result.json and the difference stated

arms.name: sc_s3c_gse
arms.role: (s3c-gse), (s3c) with the GSE cash cycle as a 19th-25th ramp

primary.metric: grid CRPS (23 levels) averaged over leads h = 1..5
primary.pressure_probability: the Brier score of P(spread > +5 bp), the probability read off the 23 quantiles as 1 - F(floor(tau) + 0.5), F linear between them (spread_mean_reversion.exceedance), the event strict and on whole basis points (data.exceeds_bp)
primary.comparisons: (s3c-gse) paired with (s3c) and with (s3), and against B1, B1' and B2

scoring.scorer: repo_model.scoring_protocol (#655), the development tier: no verdict, no registration
scoring.test: scoring_protocol.paired_tests, the studentized stationary bootstrap (ruling 1), mean block 10 business days, 10,000 draws, seed 1274, two-sided 90% interval (the lower end is the one-sided 95% bound); the skill interval and the studentized interval on mean d are reported for every tested row; where the studentized bound cannot be computed the unstudentized percentile interval of mean d is given beside it, with no reading taken from it
scoring.reading: a reading is taken from the mean-d bound (her ruling on #1009): the arm is read better than a reference when the lower end of the 90% interval of mean d is above zero, worse when the upper end is below zero, otherwise undecided. Lens C's caveat (the lag-10 HAC standard error is understated about 2x after 2020) is stated on the page
scoring.splits: per window: pooled; by lead; by regime of the target day; by pressure-day type of the target day (turn_days.reporting_day_type); by target month; and the days the changed term is non-zero (target days from the 19th to the 25th) against the other days. A group of fewer than 20 days is listed and not tested. The intervals of a group of target days keep the current method (the group's days, scattered, resampled in date order as if consecutive), which #1221 questions and #1228 will decide; the page labels them so and reads no pressure-day type from them
scoring.identical_groups: a group in which an arm's score equals the reference's on every day is listed as identical and not tested against it

coverage.band: the 90% band, q05 to q95 closed (state_calendar_1145.BANDS['b90']); the share of cells in which the realised spread lies inside it, for (s3c-gse), (s3c) and (s3), pooled and by lead, with the stationary-bootstrap interval of s3_2026_check_1222 (cells in date order, mean block in cells as that script has it for a pooled or a lead group)

effect.what: the fitted effect of the changed term in bp, by regime: for (s3c-gse), the ramp's coefficient (standardised units) of the fit in use at the decision times the scale at the decision's anchor, per unit of ramp, i.e. the shift on the 25th; for (s3), the same for the flat 19th-23rd flag. Reported as the mean over the scored (decision day, lead) cells of each regime of the target day, by lead and pooled over leads, with the share of cells whose fit holds the term and, for the cells whose target day carries the term, the mean shift actually applied (effect x scale x ramp value, or x flag). A refit's effects in standardised units are listed in result.json

event_list: none: this directive asks for the Brier score of P(> +5 bp), reported pooled and split; the counts of positive days and cells are in result.json
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; (s3c) stays the candidate until she rules on the result.
A gain or loss is read from the 90% interval of mean d excluding zero; otherwise undecided. A point estimate alone is not read.
A pooled figure is never read without the regime, pressure-day-type and ramp-day splits beside it. The pressure figures rest on few days; the page states the counts.
The page cites no source for the idea beyond her ruling and compares with no outside figure.
The page ends with marked questions for Eleonora with numbered options and defaults that change no claim.
